name: Kodak Professional Tri-X 400 (400TX)
notes: One datasheet (F-4017) covers Tri-X 400 (400TX) and Tri-X 320 (320TXP); each has its own sheet file.
Characteristic curves: x axis is absolute log exposure in lux-seconds, as printed; the exposure light (daylight/tungsten) is not stated on the sheet, 'daylight' is assumed. No Log H Ref is printed.

curves/v is the 35 mm plot with Kodak T-MAX Developer, small tank, 30 s agitation, 6 minutes: the processing table (page 3, 68 F small tank) gives 6 min for T-MAX to reach the contrast index of 0.56 the sheet recommends. Other T-MAX times on the same plot: v-tmax-7, v-tmax-9, v-tmax-11.

Plot 'curves-d76' (a second page, so a second plot): 35 mm, D-76, large tank, 1 min agitation, 6/8/10/12 min as v-d76-6, v-d76-8, v-d76-10, v-d76-12. The recommended D-76 large-tank time (7 3/4 min at 68 F, CI 0.56) lies between the 6 and 8 min curves. The 120-size plots (T-MAX and D-76, slightly lower base density) were not traced.

Spectral sensitivity: one plot for both Tri-X films, effective exposure 0.5 s, diffuse visual. sensitivity/v is the solid curve 'D=1.0 > Gross Fog'; v-d03 is the dashed curve 'D=0.3 > Gross Fog'. Log sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure (erg/cm2) as printed. Doubt: the legend gives the solid, upper curve (log sensitivity about 2.5 to 2.7) as D=1.0 and the dashed, lower one (about 1.2 to 1.6) as D=0.3, the reverse of what physics suggests (a higher density needs more exposure, so lower sensitivity); the assignment follows the legend as printed. The two curves have the same shape.

Grain: diffuse rms granularity 17 (fine), read at net diffuse density 1.0 with a 48 micrometre aperture, 12x; measured in KODAK HC-110 Developer (Dilution B), 20 C (the sheet's IMAGE STRUCTURE section). Tri-X 320 = 16.
Push: the sheet's machine-processing table lists Tri-X 400 at EI 800 (D-76 5 to 7 min, T-MAX RS 4 to 6 min, XTOL 5 to 7 min at 22 C, large-tank rack-and-tank); no curves are plotted for EI 800.
